images.alt: Eric Davis, program manager in DARPA’s Strategic Technology Office, said his entire $250 million portfolio consists of AI-related projects. However, “there's not a single large language model in the work that I'm doing right now,” he said during a keynote speech at the National Training and Simulation Association’s MODSIM World conference.

“We're told that generative AI is going to design our supply chains. It's going to coordinate our disaster response, run our power grids, do our homework for us,” he continued. The technology has massive potential, but it cannot solve every problem. 

Large language models can ingest vast amounts of data and produce well-articulated outputs that maximize one thing: human approval. “That's why what they say is so convincing,” Davis said. “What they lack are internal models of causal reality.”

These models don’t understand concepts like gravity, fluid dynamics or fuel consumption. They don’t understand how diseases are transmitted or the laws of thermodynamics. “If we ask an LLM to output a plan, we get a very convincing language-shaped, plan-shaped output. But whether it's for wildfire evacuation, a hospital surge or military planning, what it's not based on is reality,” he said. “And if we trust that plan to be truthful, we will be disappointed.”

少女は両手で、金属製のじょうろを持っている。じょうろは画面左下へ向けられ、先端から細い水の流れが無数に広がっている。水は透明というより、淡いピンク色を帯びた光沢のある液体として描かれている。

画面左上には、大きな透明な容器が置かれている。容器は円筒形で、上部には蓋があり、中には鮮やかなピンク色の飲み物が満たされている。液体にはレモンの輪切りがいくつも浮かび、泡や水滴も見える。下部には蛇口が付いており、そこからピンク色の液体が雫となって落ちている。容器の周囲には、まるで雲のような白や薄桃色の綿状のものが広がっている。

Feature Idea: ChatGPT Connect — “People You Might Connect With”

What if ChatGPT had an optional social side where it could connect you with people who share your interests?

Not another Facebook-style “People You May Know.”

Instead, ChatGPT could use age + interests to suggest people you might genuinely enjoy learning or talking with.

For example:

« Someone You Might Connect With

16 • Nigeria

AI • Python • Medicine • STEM • Chemistry • Writing

6 interests in common

[Connect] [Skip]»

If both users choose Connect, they can have a private one-to-one chat.

Profiles could include:

- Name

- Age

- Nationality

- Ethnic group/tribe (optional)

- Religion (optional)

- 6–10 interests

Users would control what is visible, and private ChatGPT conversations would remain private.

The best part?

ChatGPT itself would still remain the main experience.

You could have:

ChatGPT → Connect → Chats → Profile

So instead of only helping you find answers, ChatGPT could potentially help you find people who are interested in the same things you are.

Imagine a student interested in AI and medicine in Nigeria connecting with another student interested in medical AI somewhere else in the world.

Facebook asks:

“Who do you know?”

ChatGPT Connect could ask:

“Who might you learn and grow with?”

Obviously, strong age-based safety, privacy, consent, moderation, and protections for younger users would be essential.

I think this could make ChatGPT a really interesting combination of AI assistant + learning platform + human connection.

What do you think?

Greetings everyone, system designer .

Fortunately I have mapped most of the intricacies of the new complex low tier system recently, cause I was curious about how the tech teams made the so called “unlimited” even possible. Yeah it can be a bit confusing, cause it wasn’t clearly communicated, how things actually work now. I can explain it’s rules and can give tips, know about some workarounds, and how one can optimize settings depending on preferences. The available choices come with trade-offs. It’s basically like a building block system now, one can customize it to some extend. Other aspects are imposed. Go users will experience similar things to free users. So let’s start with the basics and walk through.

* * *

A. Basic Behavior

First of all, the conversation environment has currently two different basic modes now.

  1. The new text-only mode: is exactly how it sounds like. No other resources are allowed beyond text and text-alike tokens. That’s what PR has been selling as “unlimited text chats”. Letters, characters and emojis are fine. Search results in text form with external link sources only too. Not included are:


  * image or file uploads
  * image generation
  * image or file recalls from the library
  * in-line images the model retrieves with the search tool


  2. The old full resource mode: still exists in a somewhat different form. Various limits do apply and it is a bit more fuzzy than it used to be. The old rule of 10 interactions every 5 hours in the free tier is only true with the right settings. The 3-ish image generations per 24 hours does also still exist, even though sometimes it can be file size based and not a fixed number. I know to little about the new library related rules, but it might have been 3-ish uploads per day. I can’t tell, if stored file and stored image recall has a limit. Not my regular setting.



Behind the curtains sits a new tag system as a regulator. Every conversation environment without extra resources counts as an unlimited text-only runtime. As soon as an extra resource enters the context, the conversation gets the first of the two rate-limit tags. This transition is final and can’t be reversed. If no other higher rules apply, the old 10 exchanges very 5 hours counts. Because of the tags the system knows, which runtime mode is active and behaves accordingly. Even if one switches between conversations.

* * *

B. Advances Behavior

Now the first tricky part. The new ads system influences rate-limit behavior too. It can inflict a further reduction of 50% to the general interaction, so 10 becomes 5 for free users. Users who option out of ads or even just turn personalization off, will encounter the further reduction. This is settings based. It’s very likely that it is of higher system hierarchy than the text-only mode and will trigger despite no resources use.

The 31 new regions get at first no personalization options, nor the option-out option, as far as I know. It is in non-personalized mode by default and will be changed later. So the official statement

* * *

C. Rule Exceptions

Well, here is the even trickier part. There are some exceptions to the basic rules. If the new age predictions system maps a user under the age of 18, ads do not apply. The user can be put into teen mode, which comes with other rules. Also. If delicate topics are present, like personal health data for example, ads do not apply. These type of conversation shell be kept clean, so from official side.

* * *

D. Trade-offs

Theoretically, one can choose, which mode and interaction style one preferes and act accordingly.

  1. It is possible to use up separate daily resource limits by opening up new conversation environments. The limit triggers one exchange after the appearance of the resource, when one has used all 5-10 exchanges of the 5 hours in a full resource runtime. But I wouldn’t recommend hopping. It creates noise and fragmentation.

  2. It also is possible to disable tools like web search and library access via settings, to avoid most resource sources triggers entirely and decrease the likelihood of some rate-limit tags. One also can store a little framework in the custom instructions that would work like ASCII art enhancement and not affect image limits.




So yeah. The current new system can be a bit overwhelming. Choices matter more than ever. And one can decide what matters most, quality or quantity.

* * *

A fellow system mapper has also collect data independently, when the beta was still relatively fresh and kept observing. The new free and go tier rules have stayed pretty consistent. At that time the text-only mode did not existed yet. So the first reduction rules in terms of ads exist for a while now. It’s intentional and might further change in the future.

(https://www.aiqnahub.com/chatgpt-free-plan-chat-limit-reduced/)
